title: Proud Tek Engineering Blog: RFID, NFC, and Smart Card Technical Notes
summary: Technical notes from the Proud Tek engineering team. Most posts are written in response to recurring buyer questions: chip-family selection, reader compatibility, encoding workflows, compliance regimes, and deployment edge cases. Skim the categories below or jump straight into the latest posts to find the answer you need before sending an inquiry.
heroPoints: 90+ technical posts covering chip families, reader compatibility, encoding, and compliance.
Each post is written by Proud Tek engineering staff and reviewed against current spec sheets.
Tagged by chip family, product type, and industry vertical for fast filtering.
imageAlt: Proud Tek engineering blog: RFID and NFC technical notes

brief.label: Most-read categories
items: Chip-family selection (NTAG, MIFARE, ICODE, EM, Impinj, Alien, UCODE).
Reader compatibility notes for hotel locks, library kiosks, and access systems.

brief.label: What you will not find here
items: Generic introductions to what RFID is.

sections.title: Why we publish technical notes instead of marketing posts
sections.intro: Most B2B RFID content online is either wikipedia-style overviews or thinly disguised sales copy. Neither helps a buyer who has a real chip-or-reader compatibility question. Our blog is written for that buyer: someone with a deployment to ship, a reader to validate, or a compliance regime to satisfy.
bullets: Each post starts from a question we have actually been asked by a buyer.
Specifications come from chip-vendor datasheets and ISO standards, not from marketing pages.
Code samples and reader configurations are tested against real hardware before publication.
Posts are dated and updated when chip revisions or standards revisions invalidate older claims.
Author and reviewer bylines link back to the engineering team profiles.

sections.title: How posts are structured
sections.intro: We use a consistent format so you can scan a post for the part you need without reading the whole thing. The first 100 words always answer the question stated in the title.
bullets: Title: a specific question or claim, never a category name.
Lede: the answer in one paragraph.
Detail sections: chip behavior, reader configuration, code or workflow, edge cases.
Compliance section: relevant standards or regulations, when applicable.
Related catalog SKUs and follow-up reading at the bottom.

sections.title: Where the topics come from
sections.intro: Posts are seeded from real inquiries. When the same question shows up three times in a quarter, it usually becomes a post.
bullets: Pre-sample technical questions that delay sample shipment.
Reader-firmware quirks that surface during deployment validation.
Compliance changes (FCC, CE, EU DPP, Battery Regulation) that affect existing programs.
New chip families that change the cost or capability of an existing deployment.
Vendor-specific compatibility notes (Saflok, VingCard, Onity, Impinj, Zebra).

faq.question: How often is the blog updated?
faq.answer: Aim is one to two technical posts per month. Frequency depends on inbound question volume; quiet quarters get fewer posts, busy quarters get more. We do not publish on a fixed editorial calendar to avoid filler.

faq.question: Can I republish a post on my own site?
faq.answer: Short excerpts with attribution and a link back to the original are fine. Full reproduction needs written permission. Email info@proudtek.com if you want to discuss a syndication arrangement.

faq.question: How do you keep posts current when chips and standards change?
faq.answer: Each post has a published date and a separately tracked review date. When NXP, Impinj, or a regulator publishes a change that invalidates a claim, the affected post is updated and the review date is moved forward. Material rewrites get a corrigendum note at the top.

faq.question: Who writes the posts?
faq.answer: Posts are written by the Proud Tek engineering team and reviewed by Peter Zhang or a topic-relevant subject expert before publication. Bylines link to the author profile under /about/review-board/.
